MANAGEMENT OF BURNS 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Management Priorities 
 
* Airway / Breathing / Circulation 
* Burns < 3 hours à cool running water over the burn for 20 minutes 
* Dry the patient & keep warm 
* Burn wound cleaning and assessment 
 
* Procedural sedation to be used 
* All blisters & debris must be removed 
   - Adult - wash the burn & surrounding area with Chlorhexidine  
     solution (Hibiscrub) 
   - Child - Wash the whole patient with Chlorhexidine solution 
               - Shave the head in a child with burns to the face 
* Evaluate the depth & Total Body Surface Area (TBSA) using the     
   Lund and Browder Chart (see figure) 
* Call the trauma surgeon on call / transfer to burns unit (CHBAH Burns/CMJAH 163) 
* Temperature and glucose 
* Analgesia 
Burn Bundles of Care 
3 hours:  Patient stabilised, fluid therapy commenced & monitored, analgesia,  
wounds cleaned & dressed, surgeons informed, escharotomy  
performed if indicated (see box for indications) 
6 hours:  Transfer organized if required 
Modified Brooke Formula 
2ml x % burn x weight (kg) 
* Half the fluid in the first 8 hours then 
* Half the fluid in following 16 hours 
Ringers Lactate / Balsol 
Minor Burns 
* Partial thickness burns < 10% 
* No involvement of special areas 
 
Management 
* Analgesia: Morphine 0.1mg/kg IVI  or Fentanyl 1µg/kg IVI  
* Dressings: Flamazine or Aquacel 
* Review at SOPD / Local Clinic 
* Discharge with appropriate analgesia 
Moderate Burns 
* Partial thickness burns 10 - 14% 
* Smaller TBSA + unstable patient 
* Major involvement of special areas 
* Deep burns < 10% 
 
Management 
* Analgesia: Morphine 0.1mg/kg or Fentanyl 1µg/kg IVI  or                            
                       Ketamine 1-2mg/kg IVI or Ketamine 2-4mg/kg IMI 
* IV line 
* Venous blood gas 
* Catheter only for perineal/genital burns 
* Dressings: Flamazine or Aquacel 
* Discuss with trauma surgeon on call 
Major Burns 
* Partial thickness burns ³ 15% in adults;  ³ 10% in paediatrics 
* Deep burns ³ 10% 
* Inhalation injury 
 
Management 
* Secure the airway if needed 
* IV access and start fluid resuscitation according to Modified Brooke Formula 
* Remember maintenance fluid for children 
* Urinary catheter & NGT for all patients 
* Fluid therapy goals: Urine output 1-2 mls/kg/hr 
    Lactate clearance within 2 hours 
    CRT < 3 seconds 
* Analgesia: Morphine 0.1mg/kg or Fentanyl 1µg/kg IVI  or                                          
                      Ketamine 1-2mg/kg IVI or Ketamine 2-4mg/kg IM 
* Dressings: Flamazine or Aquacel 
* Discuss with trauma surgeon on call  
Inhalation Injury 
* Singing of facial hair, oropharyngeal inflammation 
* Wheezing, stridor, respiratory distress, RR > 30bpm, Sats < 90% 
* ABG: PaO2 < 60mmHg, CO > 10%, PF ratio < 200 mmHg 
Contents

 
 
 
               LUND AND BROWDER CHART 
 
 
Escharotomy 
 
Indications 
Circumferential burn with vascular compromise
